ruling: HAN 2026-10-09: rulebook v0 holds two rules only, the beginner floor and the week-to-week increase limit. Everything else arrives with the full research lane (PLAN-AUTHORING.md §10).
voice: Readings and limits, in Tuwa's own words. The rulebook never diagnoses, never forecasts what may happen to the body and never prescribes a session. The athlete's agent writes the plan; Tuwa checks it against these limits.

history_bands.label: None
history_bands.question: How long have you trained with a written plan?

counting.hard_set: A working set of a resistance movement with a rep target. Warm-up sets, sets under a warm-up section, timed or distance doses, and jumps, throws, sprints and drills are not hard sets.
counting.strength_session: A training day that holds at least one hard set. Sport practice, conditioning and recovery days do not count.
counting.muscle_group: The movement's primary region: legs, chest, back, shoulders, arms or core. A movement Tuwa cannot place counts toward the weekly total only.
counting.deload_week: A week whose heading or phase name contains the word deload.

rules.title: The beginner floor
rules.applies_when: The athlete's training-history band is none or under 6 months, or the plan header says phase 1 and names no history band.
rules.summary: A first plan starts at the low end of every range, a little below what the rules allow at most.

rules.title: The week-to-week increase limit
rules.summary: From one week to the next, outside a deload, the planned load or volume of the same movement and the weekly hard-set total rise by no more than 10 %.

limits.weekly_hard_sets: This week's hard sets are at most last week's total plus 10 %, rounded up to a whole set.
limits.movement_load: A movement's top load is at most last week's top load plus 10 %, or plus one 2.5 kg step when that is larger. A percentage of a max follows the same 10 %.
limits.movement_volume: A movement's sets × reps rise by at most 10 % (rounded up to a whole rep); adding one rep to each working set always fits.
limits.timed_and_distance_doses: A timed or distance dose that rises by more than 10 % is shown as a finding, not refused.
limits.deload: A deload week is skipped: the week after it is compared with the last week before it.

nsca_essentials_4.citation: Haff GG, Triplett NT (eds). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, 4th ed. NSCA / Human Kinetics, 2016.
nsca_essentials_4.supports: The program-design frame: training frequency, volume and intensity set by training status; novices start with fewer sessions and progress gradually.

acsm_2009_progression.citation: American College of Sports Medicine. Progression models in resistance training for healthy adults. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2009;41(3):687-708.
acsm_2009_progression.supports: Novice frequency of two to three sessions a week; load increases in small steps of a few percent once the target reps are met.

schoenfeld_2017_volume.citation: Schoenfeld BJ, Ogborn D, Krieger JW. Dose-response relationship between weekly resistance training volume and increases in muscle mass. J Sports Sci. 2017;35(11):1073-1082.
schoenfeld_2017_volume.supports: Weekly hard sets per muscle group as the volume unit; gains rise with volume, and around ten weekly sets sits at the lower part of the useful range.

who_2020.citation: Bull FC, et al. World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour. Br J Sports Med. 2020;54(24):1451-1462.
who_2020.supports: The floor: muscle-strengthening work on at least two days a week.

helms_2016_rir.citation: Helms ER, et al. Application of the repetitions in reserve-based rating of perceived exertion scale for resistance training. Strength Cond J. 2016;38(4):42-49.
helms_2016_rir.supports: Effort written as reps in reserve (RIR) and its link to RPE (RPE 8 = about 2 reps in reserve).
